newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Minsa raises $54.2 mln in issue.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Minsa raises $54.2 mln in issue.

text.p: Grupo Minsa, Mexico's second largest producer of corn flour, raised a total of $54.2 million in its recent simultaneous, mixed public share offer, the company said Tuesday.
Minsa said it raised $49.7 million through the completion of an initial global offering.
It offered 2,130,000 ADSs, representing 21,300,000 series "C" shares and 14,200,000 "C" shares to Mexican investors.

In global markets, it sold 1,278,000 Rule 144A ADSs to institutional buyers in the United States and 852,000 regulation "S" ADSs to buyers outside the United States and Mexico. All sold at a price of $14 per ADS. Shares in Mexico sold at 11.19 pesos per share.

As a result of over-subscription, a greenshoe option was exercised resulting in the sale of 3,195,000 series "C" shares or 319,500 ADSs, at the same offering price. This greenshoe raised a total of $4.5 million, giving the $54.2 million total, Minsa said.
The shares sold represent about 23 percent of Minsa's share capital.

"The proceeds from the offering are expected to be used by Minsa to repay principal and interest on outstanding debt, to increase corn inventories to industry standards, to increase its working capital, to fund a portion of its capital expenditure program and for other general corporate purposes," Minsa said.
Minsa has increased its share of the Mexican corn flour market to 26 percent in 1996 from 9 percent in 1993. The company owns and operates six plants in Mexico and two in the United States.
Corn flour is the basic ingredient to make tortillas, corn pancakes eaten more widely than bread in Mexico.
